newsitem.title: UK: Pearson extends gains on upgrades, results. [CORRECTED 14:12 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Pearson extends gains on upgrades, results. [CORRECTED 14:12 GMT]

text.p: Shares in Pearson Plc extended initial gains Monday afternoon as two brokerages upgraded the stock after the media group posted stronger-than-expected results, dealers said.
By 1208 GMT, the shares were up 28p to 694.
SBC Warburg raised its recommendation on the stock to "hold" from "reduce," (corrects original rating from "buy") dealers said. The analyst wasn't immediately available to provide details.
Henderson Crosthwaite media analyst Mathew Horsman said he repeated his "long-term buy" recommendation and raised his 1998 profit forecast to 290 million from 280 million stg.
While he left his 1998 figures unchanged at 320 million stg because of a likely restructuring, he said Pearson's future looked bright.
Earlier, Pearson revealed that half-year pretax profits had soared to 81 million stg from 30 million stg in the same period last year.
Profits from continuing operations almost doubled to 65.5 million stg compared with a consensus forecast of 46 million stg.

"The market is quite right to mark the shares up," Horsman said. "(Pearson executives) were very bullish at an analysts briefing and the market is reassured that the fraud situation at Penguin is close to being resolved and that there are no further black holes." --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
